column3: Do you review user access rights on a defined schedule?
column4: Yes — access reviews run quarterly across all production systems; the most recent review was completed in [month YYYY].
column5: Access Control Policy v2.1, §4; most recent quarterly access review report
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.18 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-05 / CSA CCM v4.0 IAM-08

column3: Do you have a documented incident response plan that is tested?
column4: Yes — a documented incident response plan defines severity levels and escalation paths; the most recent tabletop exercise ran in [month YYYY] and its findings were tracked to closure.
column5: Incident Response Plan v1.3; tabletop exercise notes [YYYY-MM]
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.24 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.IM-04 / CSA CCM v4.0 SEF-03, SEF-04

column3: Do you test backup restoration?
column4: Partially — automated daily backups with monthly restore verification for the primary database; a full disaster-recovery failover test is planned for [quarter YYYY], owned by the Platform Lead.
column5: Backup and Recovery Runbook; restore-verification log
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.13 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS-11 / CSA CCM v4.0 BCR-08

column3: Do you maintain a risk register reviewed by leadership?
column4: Yes — a quarterly-reviewed risk register tracks security, operational, and compliance risks with named owners and remediation timelines; the most recent leadership review was completed in [month YYYY].
column5: Risk Register v3.2; leadership review minutes [YYYY-MM]
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 6.1.2 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-06 / CSA CCM v4.0 GRC-02

column3: Is there a named owner for information security risk?
column4: Yes — the CTO is the executive owner of information security risk and chairs the quarterly risk review with the security and engineering leads.
column5: Security Governance Charter §2.1
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 5.3 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RR-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 GRC-06

column3: Do you maintain a written information security policy approved by management?
column4: Yes — the Information Security Policy is reviewed annually and approved by the executive team; the current version, v2.4, was approved in [month YYYY].
column5: Information Security Policy v2.4 (signed approval page)
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.1 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 GRC-01

column3: How often are security policies reviewed and re-approved?
column4: Annually at minimum, or sooner when a material change in scope, technology, or regulatory environment triggers an interim review.
column5: Policy Management Procedure §3.2
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.1 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-02 / CSA CCM v4.0 GRC-03

column3: Do employees receive security awareness training at hire and periodically after?
column4: Yes — security awareness training is delivered within the first 30 days of hire and refreshed annually thereafter, with role-based modules for engineering and customer-facing teams.
column5: Training completion records (LMS export, current year)
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.6.3 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AT-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 HRS-11

column3: Are background checks performed where legally permitted?
column4: Yes — third-party background checks (identity, criminal record where permitted, employment history) are completed before offer acceptance for all employees and contractors with access to customer data.
column5: Pre-employment Screening Procedure §1.4
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.6.1 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RR-04 / CSA CCM v4.0 HRS-01

column3: Do you maintain an inventory of systems that store or process customer data?
column4: Yes — a cloud-asset inventory is maintained in the CMDB and reconciled monthly against cloud-provider billing data; assets storing or processing customer data are tagged `data-class:customer`.
column5: CMDB export; most recent monthly reconciliation report
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.9 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-02 / CSA CCM v4.0 DCS-06

column3: Is customer data classified and handled according to a data classification standard?
column4: Yes — a four-tier classification standard (Public / Internal / Confidential / Restricted) governs storage, transmission, and access; customer data is Confidential by default and Restricted where it includes regulated information.
column5: Data Classification Standard v1.2
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.12 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-05 / CSA CCM v4.0 DSP-04

column3: Is multi-factor authentication enforced for remote and administrative access?
column4: Yes — MFA is enforced on all SSO-protected applications, VPN access, and administrative consoles via phishing-resistant authenticators (WebAuthn/FIDO2 primary, TOTP fallback).
column5: Identity provider configuration export; MFA enforcement policy
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.5 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-03 / CSA CCM v4.0 IAM-14

column3: Are privileged accounts separated from day-to-day user accounts?
column4: Yes — administrators use separate, named privileged accounts that are not used for email or general productivity; time-limited, just-in-time elevation through an access proxy is required for production access.
column5: Privileged Access Policy §2.3; access-proxy audit log
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.2 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-05 / CSA CCM v4.0 IAM-10

column3: Is access revoked within a defined time after termination?
column4: Yes — termination triggers a documented offboarding workflow that revokes SSO, hardware tokens, and physical access on the employee's last working day, with completion logged within 24 hours.
column5: Offboarding Runbook; HRIS-SSO deprovisioning integration logs
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.18 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 IAM-07

column3: Is code reviewed before release to production?
column4: Yes — every change requires a peer pull-request review and a passing CI gate (lint, type-check, unit and integration tests, SAST) before merge; direct pushes to production branches are blocked at the repository level.
column5: Branch protection rules export; PR audit log
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.25, A.8.28 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS-06 / CSA CCM v4.0 AIS-04

column3: Do you run security testing (SAST/DAST or penetration tests) on a defined schedule?
column4: Yes — SAST runs on every pull request, DAST runs nightly against staging, and an independent third-party penetration test is performed annually with findings triaged into the next sprint.
column5: Most recent third-party penetration test report; CI security scan history
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.29 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 AIS-05, TVM-06

column3: How are secrets and credentials managed in your build and runtime environments?
column4: Secrets are stored in the cloud provider's managed secrets service and injected at runtime via narrowly scoped roles; the build pipeline uses short-lived OIDC tokens — no long-lived credentials exist in source control or CI variables.
column5: Secrets Management Standard §2; OIDC trust policy
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.17 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-01

column3: Is network access segmented between production and corporate environments?
column4: Yes — production runs in dedicated cloud accounts isolated from corporate networks; access requires SSO, MFA and just-in-time elevation through an access proxy, with no direct corporate-to-production routes.
column5: Network architecture diagram; cloud account boundary export
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.22 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IR-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 IVS-03

column3: Are firewalls or security groups reviewed on a schedule?
column4: Yes — security groups and WAF rules are reviewed quarterly; drift between defined IaC and live configuration is detected daily via automated scans and remediated within one business day.
column5: Quarterly review log; drift-detection alerts (current quarter)
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.20 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IR-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 IVS-03

column3: Are systems hardened to a documented baseline and patched on a defined cadence?
column4: Yes — production hosts use immutable container images built from a hardened base; CVE scanning runs on every build, with critical CVEs patched within 7 days and high within 30 days per policy.
column5: Patch Management Policy §3; most recent CVE remediation report
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.8, A.8.9 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS-01, PR.PS-02 / CSA CCM v4.0 IVS-04, TVM-03

column3: Are laptops encrypted and centrally managed?
column4: Yes — all employee laptops are MDM-enrolled with full-disk encryption enforced, screen-lock policies applied, and EDR running with central alerting.
column5: MDM compliance dashboard export
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.1 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 UEM-05, UEM-08

column3: Which cloud providers and regions host customer data?
column4: Customer data is hosted on AWS in Canada: `ca-central-1` (Montréal, primary) and `ca-west-1` (Calgary, disaster recovery). No customer data is processed or stored outside these regions without explicit customer consent.
column5: Hosting Disclosure Statement v1.5
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.23 / CSA CCM v4.0 DSP-19

column3: Is customer data encrypted at rest and in transit? Which algorithms/protocols?
column4: Yes — AES-256 at rest using the cloud provider's key management service (customer-managed keys available on request) and TLS 1.2+ in transit; legacy protocols are disabled at the load balancer.
column5: Encryption Standard §1.1; external TLS configuration scan report
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS-01, PR.DS-02 / CSA CCM v4.0 CEK-03

column3: Do you maintain audit logs for production systems and review them?
column4: Yes — production application, infrastructure, and identity logs are centralised in our SIEM with 90-day hot retention and 13-month cold retention; on-call engineers triage detection alerts 24/7.
column5: Logging and Monitoring Standard; SIEM detection coverage matrix
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.15, A.8.16 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS-04, DE.CM-09 / CSA CCM v4.0 LOG-03, LOG-05

column3: Is there a documented change management process for production changes?
column4: Yes — production changes follow a documented process: peer-reviewed PR, automated test gate, staged rollout, and a documented rollback plan; emergency changes follow an expedited path with review after the fact at the next change board.
column5: Change Management Policy v2.1
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.32 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-07 / CSA CCM v4.0 CCC-01

column3: Will you notify customers of a security incident within a defined timeframe?
column4: Yes — customers are notified of confirmed security incidents affecting their data within 72 hours of detection, with regular status updates until resolution, per our contractual notification commitment.
column5: MSA §8 (Incident Notification); Incident Response Plan v1.3
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.26 / NIST CSF 2.0 RS.CO-02 / CSA CCM v4.0 SEF-07

column3: Do you have documented business continuity and disaster recovery plans?
column4: Yes — documented BC and DR plans cover personnel, facilities, and the production environment; the DR plan defines failover sequencing for the primary cloud region and is reviewed annually.
column5: Business Continuity Plan v1.4; Disaster Recovery Plan v2.0
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.29, A.5.30 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.IM-04 / CSA CCM v4.0 BCR-04, BCR-09

column3: What are your recovery time (RTO) and recovery point (RPO) objectives?
column4: Production environment: RTO 4 hours, RPO 15 minutes. Tier-2 services: RTO 8 hours, RPO 1 hour.
column5: DR Plan v2.0 §2 (RTO/RPO matrix)
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.30 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IR-03 / CSA CCM v4.0 BCR-02

column3: Do you perform vulnerability scanning and track remediation to closure?
column4: Yes — authenticated vulnerability scans run weekly against production and dependency scans run on every build; findings are tracked in our ticketing system with SLAs of 7 days (critical), 30 days (high), 90 days (medium).
column5: Vulnerability Management Standard; remediation SLA dashboard
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.8 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 TVM-03, TVM-07

column3: Do you have a privacy policy covering collection, use, and retention of personal data?
column4: Yes — a published privacy policy describes data collection, purposes, retention periods, and individuals' rights; it is reviewed annually and on material change.
column5: Privacy Policy (public, v3.1)
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.34 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.OC-03 / CSA CCM v4.0 DSP-01

column3: Do you support individuals' access, export and deletion requests within defined timelines?
column4: Yes — verified requests (access, export, deletion) are fulfilled within 30 days; requests are tracked in a dedicated workflow with audit logging of approval and completion.
column5: Privacy Request Procedure §2.4; request ticket log
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.34 / CSA CCM v4.0 DSP-11

column3: Do you assess the security of your own subprocessors and vendors?
column4: Yes — vendors with access to customer data complete a security review (a standard questionnaire plus SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence where available) before contract signing and are reassessed annually.
column5: Vendor Risk Management Procedure; vendor inventory (current quarter)
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.19, A.5.22 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.SC-06, GV.SC-07 / CSA CCM v4.0 STA-08, STA-14

column3: Will you provide your subprocessor list and notify customers of changes?
column4: Yes — the current subprocessor list is published on our trust page and customers are notified at least 30 days in advance of material changes by email and trust-page update.
column5: Subprocessor List (public trust page); Customer Notification Procedure §1
column11: CSA CCM v4.0 DSP-14

column3: Do you know which of your vendors' own subcontractors can reach customer data, and do your contracts pass security requirements down the chain?
column4: Yes for vendors that handle customer data — each must disclose its own subprocessors, which are recorded in the vendor inventory, and our agreements require equivalent security and breach-notification terms to be passed down. Beyond that tier we rely on the vendor's independent audit reports.
column5: Vendor inventory (subcontractor column); vendor agreement template §7
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.21 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.SC-05 / CSA CCM v4.0 STA-07, STA-12

column3: How do you manage security risk in third-party and open-source software components?
column4: Dependencies are pinned and scanned on every build, and a software bill of materials is generated for each release; a critical advisory in a dependency is triaged within one business day and patched under the vulnerability SLA. New packages are reviewed before first use.
column5: Dependency Management Standard; most recent release SBOM; dependency scan history
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.21 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-09 / CSA CCM v4.0 TVM-05

column3: Do you use AI or machine-learning services to process customer data, and is that use governed by policy?
column4: Yes — an AI Use Policy lists approved tools and the data types that may not be entered into them; an inventory of AI features and third-party AI services is maintained, and each new use passes a security and privacy review before launch.
column5: AI Use Policy v1.1; AI system inventory; AI review checklist
column11: No close equivalent in these three frameworks; see ISO/IEC 42001 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework

column3: Is customer data used to train or fine-tune AI models, yours or a third party's?
column4: No — customer data is not used to train or fine-tune any model. Third-party AI providers are engaged under terms that exclude training on our inputs and limit retention; both points are stated in our data processing agreement and subprocessor list.
column5: Data Processing Agreement (AI processing clause); provider data-usage terms on file
column11: No close equivalent in these three frameworks; see ISO/IEC 42001 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework

column3: How is physical access controlled at the offices and facilities that house systems or customer data?
column4: We operate no data centres: production runs in the cloud provider's facilities, whose physical controls are covered by the provider's independent audit reports, which we review annually. Our office is badge-controlled with visitor sign-in, and no customer data is stored on office premises.
column5: Cloud provider audit report review (annual); Office Access Procedure
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.7.2 / NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-06 / CSA CCM v4.0 DCS-07, DCS-09

column3: How do you track the legal, regulatory and contractual security requirements that apply to you?
column4: A compliance register lists each applicable law, regulation and contractual security commitment with its owner and the controls that satisfy it; the register is reviewed twice a year and whenever a new customer contract adds an obligation.
column5: Compliance Register; contract obligations tracker
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.31 / NIST CSF 2.0 GV.OC-03 / CSA CCM v4.0 GRC-07

column3: Is your security programme independently assessed?
column4: Yes — an independent auditor assesses the security programme annually and the report is available under NDA; findings are tracked to closure in the risk register. An internal control review runs between audits.
column5: Most recent independent audit report; audit findings tracker
column11: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.35 / NIST CSF 2.0 ID.IM-01 / CSA CCM v4.0 A&A-02
